summary: Dan Cleary, co-founder of PromptHub—a prompt management tool for teams to test, collaborate, and deploy prompts—delivers a concise session on three prompt engineering tactics at the AI Engineer Summit 2023. He frames the problem: while simply stating what you want to an LLM often yields decent results, the non-deterministic nature of these models means small prompt changes can have outsized effects on outputs. This fragility is especially risky for products integrating AI, where a single off-the-rails response can damage brand trust and result in loss of user trust. Users now have high expectations shaped by easy ChatGPT access—expecting crisp, accurate, hallucination-free, fast outputs. The first tactic is Multi-Persona Prompting, from the University of Illinois. It calls on various agents designed for a specific task to collaborate in a brainstorming mechanism with the AI leading. For example, prompting a model to help write a book would introduce personas like a publicist, an author, and the target audience, who go back and forth until reaching a final answer. Dan finds it especially useful for complex or generative tasks because the full collaboration process is visible. The second tactic is the According to Method, from Johns Hopkins University. It grounds prompts to a specific source by appending phrases like 'according to Wikipedia' to questions, increasing the chance the model retrieves from that source and reducing hallucinations by up to 20%. It suits fine-tuned or general models reaching for a consistent data source. The third tactic is the Emotion Prompt, researched by Microsoft and other universities. It examines how LLMs react to emotional stimuli at the end of prompts, tying into cognitive behavior—like a boss emphasizing a task's importance making you take it more seriously. Adding a simple emotional stimulus can improve outputs, with experiments showing 8% to 115% increases depending on the task. Dan has seen improvements from cover letters to changelogs. All three methods are available as templates on prompthub.us.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Motivation
sections.summary: Dan introduces himself as co-founder of PromptHub, a prompt management tool for teams. He explains why prompt engineering matters: LLMs are non-deterministic, small prompt changes cause outsized effects, and one bad AI experience in a product can damage brand trust. Users have high expectations shaped by ChatGPT access—expecting crisp, accurate, fast, hallucination-free outputs.

sections.title: Multi-Persona Prompting
sections.summary: First tactic from the University of Illinois. Calls on various agents designed for a specific task to collaborate in a brainstorming mechanism with the AI leading. Example: prompting to write a book would generate personas like publicist, author, and target audience. Especially useful for complex or generative tasks because the full collaboration process is visible.

sections.title: According to Method
sections.summary: Second tactic from Johns Hopkins University. Grounds prompts to a specific source by appending phrases like 'according to Wikipedia.' Increases the chance the model retrieves from that source and can reduce hallucinations by up to 20%. Suited for fine-tuned or general models reaching for a consistent data source.

sections.title: Emotion Prompt
sections.summary: Third tactic from Microsoft and other universities. Examines how LLMs react to emotional stimuli at the end of prompts, tying into human cognitive behavior. Adding a simple emotional stimulus can improve outputs, with experiments showing 8% to 115% increases depending on the task. Dan's favorite tactic; has seen improvements from cover letters to changelogs.

sections.title: Closing and Resources
sections.summary: All three methods are available as templates on prompthub.us for copying, running in a playground, sharing with teams, or using via API links. Dan invites questions and offers to chat further.
